hints: Focus on the possible positions where two H atoms and two Br atoms can add across the four carbons of buta-1,3-diene.
Identify the three structurally isomeric dibromobutane products formed by 1,2- and 1,4-electrophilic addition: 1,3-dibromobutane, 2,3-dibromobutane, and 2,2-dibromobutane.
Inspect each of the three dibromobutane isomers for a carbon bonded to four different groups to count how many possess at least one chiral centre.
walkthrough:
**Identify the three structural isomers**

Adding 2 moles of $\text{HBr}$ across buta-1,3-diene $(\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2)$ gives dibromobutanes $(\text{C}_4\text{H}_8\text{Br}_2)$. Electrophilic addition can yield three distinct structural isomers:

$$\text{1. } \text{CH}_2\text{Br}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CHBr}-\text{CH}_3 \quad \text{(1,3-dibromobutane)}$$
$$\text{2. } \text{CH}_3-\text{CHBr}-\text{CHBr}-\text{CH}_3 \quad \text{(2,3-dibromobutane)}$$
$$\text{3. } \text{CH}_3-\text{CBr}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3 \quad \text{(2,2-dibromobutane)}$$

**Check 1,3-dibromobutane for chirality**

In 1,3-dibromobutane, carbon-3 is bonded to four different groups: $-\text{H}$, $-\text{Br}$, $-\text{CH}_3$, and $-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$. Therefore, C3 is a chiral centre.

**Check 2,3-dibromobutane and 2,2-dibromobutane for chirality**

In 2,3-dibromobutane, both carbon-2 and carbon-3 are bonded to four different groups: $-\text{H}$, $-\text{Br}$, $-\text{CH}_3$, and $-\text{CHBrCH}_3$. Thus, 2,3-dibromobutane has two chiral centres.
In 2,2-dibromobutane, carbon-2 has two identical $-\text{Br}$ atoms, and neither C1, C3, nor C4 has four different groups. So 2,2-dibromobutane has 0 chiral centres.

**Conclude the count**

Of the three structural isomers, exactly two (1,3-dibromobutane and 2,3-dibromobutane) possess at least one chiral centre.

options.A: Incorrect. 1,3-dibromobutane has a chiral centre at C3, and 2,3-dibromobutane has chiral centres at C2 and C3, so the count cannot be 0.
options.B: Incorrect. This assumes only one product is chiral (typically 1,3-dibromobutane), overlooking that 2,3-dibromobutane also contains chiral centres.
options.C: Correct. Exactly two of the three structural isomers (1,3-dibromobutane and 2,3-dibromobutane) contain at least one chiral centre. 2,2-dibromobutane has no chiral centres.
options.D: Incorrect. 2,2-dibromobutane has two identical bromine atoms on C2, so it has no chiral centre. Therefore, not all three products are chiral.
